s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute respiratory and systemic illness in an immunocompromised host
salient_findings: Subjective fevers, shortness of breath, and worsening cough for 6 days
key_facts: 50-year-old man
Common variable immunodeficiency (CVID) with intravenous immunoglobulin therapy
HIV with undetectable viral load and CD4 count 140 cells/µL
Chronic bronchiectasis with history of Mycobacterium avium complex pulmonary infection
Recurrent giardiasis
Myopathy treated with long-term low-dose prednisone
Recurrent herpes simplex virus infections
Oxygen saturation 97% on room air
CD4 count 140 cells/µL
HIV viral load undetectable
Viral resistance testing showed mutations in UL97 and UL54 genes
Elevated CMV viral load during hospital admission

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated CMV viral load and immunocompromised state

shortlist.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: History of Pneumocystis prophylaxis and immunocompromised state

shortlist.label: Mycobacterium avium complex infection
shortlist.why_kept: History of Mycobacterium avium complex pulmonary infection and chronic bronchiectasis

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated CMV viral load and gastrointestinal symptoms possible in immunocompromised patients

shortlist.label: Invasive aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic bronchiectasis and immunocompromised state increase risk for opportunistic infections

raw.rationale: Elevated CMV viral load during hospital admission and mutations in UL97 and UL54 genes indicating viral resistance, along with the patient's immunocompromised state due to HIV and CVID, support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
rejected.why: Patient was on trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole for Pneumocystis prophylaxis and CT scan showed no consolidations or ground-glass opacities

rejected.label: Mycobacterium avium complex infection
rejected.why: Patient has a history of this infection but current presentation and lab results do not specifically indicate an active MAC infection

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus colitis
rejected.why: While CMV colitis is possible, the patient's symptoms and elevated CMV viral load more strongly suggest a pulmonary involvement

rejected.label: Invasive aspergillosis
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence provided in the vignette to support this diagnosis, such as characteristic radiographic findings or positive cultures
